info.title: SoyMutDB
info.description:
SoyMutDB API — high-performance multi-species genomic variant platform
(soybean currently the default species).

## Error contract

Every error response uses the unified envelope (see `ErrorResponse`):

```json
{
  "error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "...", "details": {}},
  "request_id": "…",
  "status_code": 404
}
```

- `request_id` is always present and echoed in the `X-Request-ID` header.
- Validation failures (422) additionally return a field-level `errors` array
  (`ValidationErrorResponse`); internal framework structures are never
  exposed.
- 500 responses never include stack traces, SQL, paths, or exception text.

## Authentication

- **Bearer**: JWT access tokens via `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
  (obtained from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`).
- **Cookie**: refresh sessions use the HttpOnly `soymutdb_refresh` cookie
  (path-scoped to `/api/v1/auth`) for `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` and
  `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`.

post.description:
Register a new user account (Argon2id password hashing).

Password strength is validated both client-side and server-side.

Authenticate and return an access token (refresh token via cookie).

Login attempts are limited through the shared Redis-backed fixed-window
limiter before credential verification. This keeps the limit consistent
across workers and instances without changing the authentication flow.

The refresh token is set as an HttpOnly cookie scoped to ``/api/v1/auth``
and is **not** included in the JSON response body.  Requests without a
trusted Origin/Referer are rejected (CSRF defence).

429.description: Rate limit exceeded; retry after the indicated number of seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until this login attempt may be retried.

post.description:
Rotate the refresh cookie into a new access/refresh pair.

The presented refresh token is read **only** from the HttpOnly cookie
(path-scoped to ``/api/v1/auth``).  Rotation is server-side: the old
token is revoked and a replacement is issued in the same family.  A
previously rotated token presented again triggers reuse detection and
revokes the whole family.  Requests without a trusted Origin/Referer
are rejected (CSRF defence).

Logout: revoke the current refresh family and clear the cookie.

Requires a valid Bearer access token.  The refresh cookie (if present)
identifies the family to revoke; the response also expires the cookie on
the client.  Requests without a trusted Origin/Referer are rejected
(CSRF defence).

get.description:

post.description:
Change the current user's password.

.. note::
    **Admin password policy** — Administrator account passwords are set
    **only** via the initial configuration (``SOYMUTDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD``
    environment variable) or the ``create_admin.py`` CLI script.
    There is **no** "forgot password" reset flow for administrator accounts.

    Non-admin users can freely change their own password through this
    endpoint. Administrators may also use it, but if they lock themselves
    out the password must be reset by a system administrator using the
    CLI script.

Server-side password strength validation is applied to the new password.

get.description: List genes with cursor pagination or the portal's page contract.

Every gene in a coordinate window, with its modelled structure.

This is what the portal's own genome view needs in order to show a locus
rather than a gene: the genes that overlap the window, each with its
transcripts and their typed ``cds`` / ``utr5`` / ``utr3`` segments. Before
this endpoint the only genome picture the API could produce was centred on
one gene (``/{gene_id}/genome-view.svg``), so "what surrounds this insertion
site" had no answer.

Declared **before** ``/{gene_id}`` on purpose: FastAPI matches routes in
declaration order, and the parameterised route would otherwise swallow
``region-structure`` as a gene accession and 404.

``gene_id`` is the assembly-scoped accession. When it exists in
multiple assemblies, ``assembly_id`` is required; the API returns an
explicit disambiguation error otherwise.

Domain errors (e.g. ``NotFoundError``) propagate to the error envelope;
unexpected exceptions are converted to a 500 HTTP error so the client
always receives a structured response.

Serve the gene's genome picture as a finished SVG.

Rendering this on the server removes the track layout from first paint and
turns the picture into an ordinary cacheable image: the browser (and any
shared cache) can reuse it across visits, and the gene page still shows a
picture before its JavaScript has run.

Window defaults to the gene body plus a quarter-span flank, matching the
portal component. ``start``/``end`` override it for a zoomed request.

Not cached: an assembly with a wrong gene count is worse than an assembly
fetched twice, and the numbers change when data is imported rather than on
their own.

Stream job status updates as Server-Sent Events.

Event format (one per updated job)::

    event: job_update
    data: {"job_type": "blast", "job_id": "...", "status": "running",
           "updated_at": "2026-08-09T12:00:00+00:00"}

When no job changed in the last poll cycle a ``: ping`` heartbeat
comment line is emitted instead.  The stream ends when the client
disconnects.

post.description:
LD heatmap data: variant coordinates + r² matrix.

- Region/gene mode returns the variant coordinates in the interval
  (from ``variant_facts``) together with ``r_squared: null`` when no
  per-sample genotype data is available (the store only carries allele
  frequencies).
- Inline ``genotypes`` mode (sample × variant dosage matrix) computes the
  full pairwise r² matrix (squared Pearson correlation of dosages).

Nucleotide diversity (π) and Watterson's θ for a gene / interval.

π = Σ 2·p·(1−p) over polymorphic sites, per base pair; θ = S / a_n is
reported when ``sample_size`` is provided.  Optional ``window_size``
(bp) returns per-window π for sliding-window plots.

post.description:
Submit an asynchronous export job (vcf/tsv/csv/json/bed).

The job is bound to exactly one assembly namespace: a named assembly
wins, otherwise the resolved release's own assembly scope is used, and a
request with neither is refused. See ``filters.assembly`` for the exact
rule and its limits.

422.description: Validation Error. The export is refused and nothing is queued, either because the request body failed schema validation (field-level ``errors`` are listed) or because the request could not be bound to exactly one assembly namespace: no assembly was named and the resolved release declares no scope, the resolved assembly name is longer than the export record can store (at most 64 characters), or the resolved release publishes no variants in that assembly namespace. A domain refusal carries the unified envelope with ``error.code`` ``validation_error`` and no ``errors`` list.

release rather than an arbitrary caller-supplied id.

get.description:
Variant density across a chromosome in the published release.

Density is computed entirely from the PostgreSQL ``variant_facts``
projection, so an unavailable projection is reported as
capability-unavailable (503). The response model also requires a concrete
``chromosome_length``: fabricating ``0`` here would both violate the
contract and present an empty chromosome as a real result. The query is
bound to the resolved release, so bins can never mix drafts into a
published density.

existing clients keep working.

AssemblyMetric.description:
One assembly-level statistic, with the reason it is unknown.

``value`` is ``None`` whenever the number could not be derived from the
authoritative tables, and a machine-readable ``reason`` then says why. It is
never defaulted to ``0``: an assembly whose annotation was never imported and
an assembly that genuinely has no genes are different facts, and once both
are printed as zero nobody can tell them apart. The two fields are mutually
exclusive on purpose -- a number with a reason ("we did not count it, but
here it is") would be a contradiction.

AssemblyStatistics.title: AssemblyStatistics
AssemblyStatistics.description:
Counts derived from real rows, scoped to one assembly.

Every number here is a ``COUNT``/``SUM`` over rows that carry an
``assembly_id`` of their own. Nothing is read from ``Release.gene_count`` or
any other denormalised counter: a release owns several assemblies, so a
release-level total copied onto each assembly would report the whole
release's genes once per assembly.

Each count is an :class:`AssemblyMetric` rather than a bare ``int`` so that
"we could not count this" survives the trip to the client. A histogram over
an empty assembly and an assembly whose statistics were never computed both
used to arrive as ``0``; with the metric shape the second arrives as
``{"value": null, "reason": "..."}`` and the page can say so.

``download_count`` is always unknown. ``download_files`` has no assembly
column -- it is linked to a release and its ``category`` is free text -- so
there is no relation to aggregate over. Guessing an assembly from a category
string would invent a number, and borrowing the release's download total
would be the same mistake as borrowing its gene count.

All five fields are required on purpose. A default of ``AssemblyMetric()``
is ``value=None, reason=None``, which the metric's own validator rejects, so
a defaulted field could not even be constructed -- and any value that *did*
construct would be an unstated measurement. Requiring them moves "somebody
forgot to say" from the reader's guess to a schema error at write time.

``assembly_id`` is mandatory: both annotations and the statistical
background must be scoped to the selected assembly.
``genes`` are gene ids (e.g. ``Glyma.01G000100``); duplicates are
tolerated and deduplicated server-side.  ``mode`` selects between the
classic over-representation test (default, backwards compatible) and the
rank-based GSEA mode.  ``values`` (one per gene, e.g. log2 fold-changes)
is required in ``gsea`` mode and must align with ``genes`` 1:1.

ExpressionRecord.description: One expression measurement. Absent values stay absent, never 0.

ExternalArticlePlatform.title: ExternalArticlePlatform
ExternalArticlePlatform.description: Approved external article origins for an explicit editor preview.

ExternalArticlePreviewRequest.title: ExternalArticlePreviewRequest
ExternalArticlePreviewRequest.description:
One explicit, review-only fetch of an approved external article URL.

The endpoint never persists or publishes content.  The caller must apply
the sanitized preview to a news form and save it through normal CMS review.

ExternalArticlePreviewResponse.title: ExternalArticlePreviewResponse
ExternalArticlePreviewResponse.description: Sanitized result of an external article preview fetch.

FamilyDetailResponse.title: FamilyDetailResponse
FamilyDetailResponse.description:
A family with its members and per-species coverage.

``coverage`` names every species the release knows about for this family,
including species with no row (``state="no_data"``), so a presence/absence
view can be drawn without the client inventing the missing species.

FooterContentResponse.title: FooterContentResponse
FooterContentResponse.description: Variant-specific, plain-text footer content and visible navigation.

FooterNavigationGroup.description: A bilingual group of footer links.

GenotypeMatrix.title: GenotypeMatrix
GenotypeMatrix.description:
Inline genotype matrix for LD computation.

``sample_ids`` (rows) × ``variant_ids`` (columns); each value is the
allele dosage (0/1/2).  Missing genotypes are not allowed – complete
rows are required (the service rejects matrices with missing calls).

GwasFileType.title: GwasFileType
GwasFileType.description: Input file family (``snp`` = EMMAX-style per-SNP phenotype format).

GwasJobResponse.title: GwasJobResponse
GwasJobResponse.description:
Job status envelope; ``result`` is the worker-written summary once the
job completes (MinIO object keys + association statistics), ``None``
otherwise.

GwasJobStatus.title: GwasJobStatus
GwasJobStatus.description:
Job status values – BLAST-style spelling aligned with the shared state
machine.

GwasResultResponse.title: GwasResultResponse
GwasResultResponse.description:
Status-aware result envelope for a GWAS job.

Completed jobs carry pre-signed download URLs for the Manhattan data
JSON, the QQ data JSON and the self-contained ``Manhattan_QQ.html``
report (all stored under ``gwas/{job_id}/output/`` in MinIO).

HomeContentResponse.title: HomeContentResponse
HomeContentResponse.description:
Editable homepage welcome block backed by ``system_settings``.

Values are rich HTML (``home.*`` keys) — the public endpoint re-runs
``sanitize_rich_html`` on read so even rows written outside the admin
settings API can never serve untrusted markup.

HomepageStats.title: HomepageStats
HomepageStats.description: Aggregate statistics shown on the public home page.

InternalMutantSearchItem.title: InternalMutantSearchItem
InternalMutantSearchItem.description:
Internal-search mutant hit: both identities plus the matched field.

Only served by the authenticated internal search endpoint; never by
external routes.

LdRequest.title: LdRequest
LdRequest.description:
LD query: a region (or gene) plus an optional inline genotype matrix.

The ``variant_facts`` store carries per-variant allele frequencies but no
per-sample genotype calls, so pairwise r² cannot be derived from the
database alone: clients that hold genotype data supply it inline via
``genotypes``; without it the response returns ``r_squared: null`` with a
``note`` explaining what is needed (the variant coordinates are still
returned for plotting).

LiteratureRecord.title: LiteratureRecord
LiteratureRecord.description: One publication, identified by DOI/PMID rather than its row key.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
Credentials for logging in — accepts email or username.

Both ``username`` and ``email`` keys are accepted; ``email`` is treated
as an alias for ``username`` so API clients may send either field.

MarkReadRequest.title: MarkReadRequest
MarkReadRequest.description: Mark a subset of notifications read (``ids``) or all of them (``all``).

MarkReadResponse.title: MarkReadResponse
MarkReadResponse.description: Number of rows flipped to read.

MatchType.title: MatchType
MatchType.description:
How a search hit matched the query.

``exact`` — canonical identifier equality; ``alias`` — curated alias
equality; ``cross_version`` — provenance-bearing cross-assembly mapping;
``text`` — substring/prose match. Never inferred from similarity alone.

MediaAssetCompleteRequest.title: MediaAssetCompleteRequest
MediaAssetCompleteRequest.description: Complete a presigned upload after the object reached S3/MinIO.

MediaAssetUpdateRequest.title: MediaAssetUpdateRequest
MediaAssetUpdateRequest.description: Editable accessibility metadata; object identity is immutable.

MemberComparisonResponse.title: MemberComparisonResponse
MemberComparisonResponse.description:
Two families side by side: shared and unique members.

``shared`` is set intersection of gene accessions; ``only_left`` /
``only_right`` are the differences. Species coverage is reported per side so
a species missing from one family is visible as ``no_data``, not as "absent
from the comparison".

MutantLineResponse.title: MutantLineResponse
MutantLineResponse.description:
Compact public mutant-line representation.

``public_id`` is the canonical external identity. The private
persistence key is never part of this public contract.

NotificationListResponse.title: NotificationListResponse
NotificationListResponse.description: Paginated notification list (unread first) plus counters.

OntologyRelationshipGraphEdge.title: OntologyRelationshipGraphEdge
OntologyRelationshipGraphEdge.description: A relation whose endpoints both occur in the bounded node projection.

OrthologRecord.description:
One directional ortholog/paralog assertion.

measurement, not an orthology assignment, and this record exists only for
rows the source itself classified.

PageDefinitionUpdate.title: PageDefinitionUpdate

for genes, ``public_id`` for mutant lines. Private persistence keys are
never placed here.

``mutant_line_public_id`` is the line's public identifier. The inventory row
id and the mutant line's internal key are persistence details and are not
part of the external contract.

shows "how many people asked for this material", which is demand signal, not
personal data. Anything that could identify a requester stays behind
``/admin/seed-requests``.

SeedRequestStatsResponse.title: SeedRequestStatsResponse
SeedRequestStatsResponse.description: Public aggregate counts keyed by gene ID.

10 MiB are stored in S3 and returned as a pre-signed ``download_url``
instead (``sequence`` is ``None`` and ``truncated`` is ``False`` – the
payload is complete, just delivered out-of-band).

SequenceAvailability.title: SequenceAvailability
SequenceAvailability.description:
Per-molecule availability for a gene's sequences.

The platform currently has no FASTA store: ``genes``/``transcripts`` carry
coordinates, not residues. Rather than fabricate a ``sequence`` string (a
gene page that silently shows a made-up nucleotide string is worse than one
that says "not imported"), the contract reports availability plus the
reason. When a sequence store is added, only ``availability`` flips and
the residue fields populate — consumers do not change shape.

SpeciesCoverageResponse.description:
Per-species presence in one family.

no member row exists -- never 0 with ``state="available"``, because that
would turn "not imported/not present" into a measured zero.

StaticBuildRequest.title: StaticBuildRequest
StaticBuildRequest.description:

against a release, so an unknown (or foreign-release) ID has to reach the
build exactly as the administrator wrote it and simply not be counted.

``packages/genome-view`` places ``cds`` / ``utr5`` / ``utr3`` boxes and the
